approach: Add `check_behavior_test_reading` to crates/athena-core/src/reading/surveys.rs, gated by the existing `changes_code_with_behavior_criterion`, and wire it as one `step!` line directly after `step!(check_code_survey(reading))` in checks.rs. The four parts are matched on labelled assumptions: `Gate order:` (a), `Existing code:` (b, the label the codebase already uses), `Record kind:` (c) and `Direct check:` (d). One generic `assumptions_labeled` helper replaces the three copies of the label filter. Revision 3 changes the following. (1) Part (c) no longer repeats `check_code_survey`. `check_code_survey` runs first and already refuses a record or data deliverable whose survey names no record evidence (surveys.rs:217-230), so the new check's (c) only compares the `Record kind:` clause with the deliverable list. The dead deliverable-path branch is removed. (2) A negation carries across a coordinated list of matches joined by `or`, `nor`, `and` or a comma. (3) The criterion collector defines its accepted forms: `criterion N`, `criteria N-M`, and lists. (4) A (d) identifier must be function-like (`_`, `::` or `name()`), and a run command never counts. (5) The negator list is moved into one shared constant that `requires_existing_code_section` also uses. The bare `than` is dropped, and only `rather than` counts. All problems are gathered into one error that names the parts and the check, so the `refuse:` line of `athena check-reading` shows it. AC4 on real readings is measured by `loop_replay` (run/mod.rs:2294) and the verification replay. The fixture replay test covers mechanics only. status.rs, verify.rs and replay.rs are listed in `unchanged_planned_files`. No prompt file, record, athena.toml, defaults.toml or workflow is touched.

decisions.choice: Part (b) is satisfied by an `Existing code:` assumption (found with `existing_code_assumptions`) that names a `crates/` path the job does not create (`names_existing_path` over the created paths) and holds one code identifier (broad definition: function-like token, or a single-token backticked word). A new generic `assumptions_labeled(reading, label)` helper is added, and `code_surveys`, `environment_assumptions` and `existing_code_assumptions` are rewritten to call it. Parts (a), (c) and (d) use the new labels `Gate order:`, `Record kind:` and `Direct check:`.
decisions.reason: Round 2 finding 1. `existing_code_assumptions` (surveys.rs:1329-1336) already parses `Existing code:` and `check_design_existing_code` uses it for reuse, so a reading that states reuse the usual way is not refused for (b), and fewer new labels means a smaller newly refused share. Three copies of one filter (surveys.rs:117-124, 605-612, 1329-1336) become one function.

rejected.option: Add a new `Reuses:` label
rejected.why: A reading that already states reuse under `Existing code:` would be refused for a label no past reading used.

rejected.option: Free prose in the `Code survey:` text
rejected.why: Prose cannot tell the error which part is missing, and AC2 needs the missing part named.

decisions.choice: Part (a) needs a `Gate order:` body with at least two code identifiers and a stop-gate phrase (`stop gate`, `stops at`, `stops after`, `stop at`, `stops before`). For (a) and (b) an identifier is a token with `_` or `::`, a word directly followed by `()`, or a backticked single token without whitespace. Tokens with `/` or a file extension never count. Part (c), revised for finding 1: the reading needs a `Record kind:` assumption. Its body either satisfies `names_record_evidence` (so it names `check_record_file`, `AnyRecord`, or a round-trip test by name or path, and the round-trip test is thereby the deliverable evidence), or is `none` and then no deliverable satisfies `is_record_or_data_deliverable`. `Record kind: none` beside a record or data deliverable is refused as a contradiction that names (c) and the file. The new check does not decide whether the survey names record evidence; `check_code_survey` runs first and does. The contradiction fixtures therefore carry a `Code survey:` that names `check_record_file`, so `check_code_survey` passes and the new check is the refuser. The round-trip-deliverable-path branch of the earlier plan is removed.
decisions.reason: Finding 1. check_code_survey (surveys.rs:217-230) reads only the survey text and refuses any record deliverable whose survey lacks record evidence, and it runs before the new step in checks.rs. So whenever a record deliverable reaches the new check, the survey already names evidence, and a branch that accepted a round-trip deliverable path could never be the one that satisfies (c). The only contradiction left for (c) is the clause saying `none` against a record deliverable. AC3's 'no accepted record kind and no round-trip test deliverable' is refused in two places by design: with no survey evidence by `check_code_survey` (a new corpus case pins this and expects Refuse("check_code_survey")), and with survey evidence but `Record kind: none` by the new check. Single-word entry points such as `replay` (replay.rs:365) stay valid for (a) when backticked.

rejected.option: Keep the round-trip-deliverable-path alternative in (c)
rejected.why: Dead branch: a record deliverable never reaches the new check without survey evidence, so the alternative can never decide the outcome.

rejected.option: Re-check record evidence from the survey inside the new check
rejected.why: It duplicates check_code_survey and would make the new check the refuser for fixtures that the earlier check already refuses.

rejected.option: Accept `Record kind: none` always
rejected.why: A new record file with `none` is the contradiction AC3 requires the check to refuse.

rejected.option: Count only tokens with `_` or `::` in (a)
rejected.why: A single-word entry point or gate never counts, so correct readings would be refused.

decisions.choice: Part (d): each non-routine behavior criterion must be named in a `Direct check:` body, and that body must hold at least one function-like identifier: a token with `_` or `::`, or a word directly followed by `()`. A plain backticked word does not count for (d). Before scanning, the check deletes every backtick span that starts `cargo ` or `athena `, and in unbackticked text deletes the word `cargo` through the end of its clause (next `;`, or `.` followed by a space). Tokens with `/`, a leading `-`, or a file extension never count. So `Direct check: criterion 2: `cargo test -p athena-core`` is refused for (d), as is the same text unbackticked. Criterion naming forms recognised by `criterion_numbers(body)`, on lowercase text: `criterion N`; `criteria N-M` (a hyphen or `to` between two numbers, an inclusive range); and lists after `criterion` or `criteria`: `criteria N, M and K`, `criteria N, M`, `criteria N and M`, `criteria N or M`. The list continues while the next token after a separator is a number; the first non-number ends it. A `criterion` word may appear several times in the body and the numbers are united. `CLAUSES` in the test helper uses `criteria 1-4`, and one unit test per form pins each of the three forms. A skip switch is matched by a closed list: the exact names `skip_probe` and `ATHENA_NO_PROBE`, plus upper-case tokens that start `ATHENA_NO_` or `ATHENA_SKIP_` (case-sensitive). Lower-case identifiers that merely contain `skip_` or `_skip` never match. An internal-helper read is matched by the phrases `internal helper`, `private helper`, `stand-in`, `through a helper` and `via a helper`. A match is refused unless negated.
decisions.reason: Findings 3 and 4 and round-2 findings 2 and 7. A critic Grep found 208 `skip_`/`_skip` identifiers in 43 files, including production `skip_note` (crates/athena-core/src/checks.rs:271), so a direct check calling `skip_note` is legitimate; `skip_probe` and `ATHENA_NO_PROBE` come from the request. A closed list is testable and its limit can be stated; the reading checks read the Reading only (surveys.rs:310-311), so the list cannot be checked against code. A `cargo test` command, or a test name passed to it, measures nothing about the property and is the indirect check the request wants refused, so commands are removed before the identifier scan. The accepted criterion forms are defined so the fixture and the real readings use the same text.

rejected.option: Count any backticked span as a (d) identifier
rejected.why: A command-only `Direct check:` would pass, though it names no function that measures the property.

rejected.option: Match any token containing `skip_` or `_skip`
rejected.why: It refuses real function names such as `skip_note`.

rejected.option: Leave the criterion forms undefined
rejected.why: A fixture written `criteria 1-4` would not match a collector for `criterion N`.

rejected.option: Detect switches by reading the repository
rejected.why: The reading checks have no repository access.

decisions.choice: Negation (revised for findings 2 and 5). One shared `pub(super) const NEGATORS: [&str; 7] = ["no","not","never","without","nothing","nor","cannot"]` is defined in surveys.rs, with the existing `n't` and `n\u{2019}t` normalisation. `requires_existing_code_section` (surveys.rs:1359-1394) is changed to use that constant; its members and behavior are unchanged and its tests run unchanged. The new check uses the same constant. `than` counts as a negator only directly after `rather` (the pair `rather than`). `instead` and `avoid` are not negators. Tokens split on whitespace, with `,` as its own token and `.`, `;`, `(`, `)`, quotes and backticks trimmed. For a match at token i, `negated(i)` walks back: skip determiners and modifiers (`a`, `an`, `the`, `any`, `internal`, `private`, `helper`), then at most one connective (`through`, `via`, `using`, `with`, `by`, `of`), then skip determiners again, and read token j. If j is a negator, the match is negated. If j is a joiner (`or`, `nor`, `and`, `,`) and the token before it (skipping determiners) is itself a match, return `negated` of that earlier match, so the negation carries across a coordinated list. In every other case the match is not negated. A joiner not preceded by a match breaks the chain, so `not through skip_probe, and ATHENA_NO_PROBE is set` is refused. Accepted by test: `without skip_probe or ATHENA_NO_PROBE`, `not through skip_probe nor ATHENA_NO_PROBE`, `no skip_probe, no helper stand-in`, `not through a helper`, `without ATHENA_NO_PROBE`. Refused by test and pinned under Limits: `no probe runs when skip_probe is set`, `faster than skip_probe`, `not through skip_probe, and ATHENA_NO_PROBE is set` (the second switch is the refused one). The Limits text and the CHANGELOG state the closed switch list, that another name or a switch described in prose is not caught, and these false cases.
decisions.reason: Finding 2: ordinary negated lists such as `without skip_probe or ATHENA_NO_PROBE` must be accepted, as AC3 requires for a negated mention, while a negator that only appears earlier in the sentence must not excuse a later switch. Finding 5: requires_existing_code_section (surveys.rs:1370) already has a NEGATORS list, so one shared list serves both reading checks and the new check adds no third list with different members. verify.rs:1261-1380 holds a clause-level negator for verifier claims; it works on different text (claims against diffs), so it is not shared and verify.rs stays unchanged. A bare `than` would accept `faster than skip_probe`, so it is dropped in favor of `rather than`.

rejected.option: A third, separate negator list including `than`, `instead`, `avoid`
rejected.why: Duplicates the list at surveys.rs:1370 and accepts `faster than skip_probe`.

rejected.option: A fixed four-token negation window
rejected.why: It accepted `no probe runs when skip_probe is set`.

rejected.option: Strictly 'negator directly before the match' with no list carry
rejected.why: It refuses `without skip_probe or ATHENA_NO_PROBE`, the natural way to write a negated mention.

rejected.option: Move or reuse the verify.rs `is_negator`
rejected.why: It is clause-level logic for another input and would change verify.rs behavior; AC8 forbids unrelated changes.

decisions.choice: A criterion is routine, and needs no direct check, when after stripping every whitespace token that starts with `-` (flags) and every token that starts `athena-` (crate names), the remaining words, split on non-alphanumerics and lower-cased, are all in a stop list: cargo, fmt, clippy, test, tests, check, pass, passes, passing, and, the, on, final, tree, still, all, locked, same, as, a, recorded, athena, workspace, warnings, targets, no, unrelated, behavior, changes, change, existing, run. The criterion must also hold a pass word and at least one of fmt, clippy or test(s). A `No unrelated behavior changes; the existing tests pass` clause is routine; the doc comment says so. Parts (a)-(c) are still required for such a reading. The producer copies the code_health.rs:529 and steward.rs:622-623 strings verbatim into corpus cases, with this reading's criterion 8.
decisions.reason: Round-2 finding 4. Tokenizing `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` yields `d`, `targets` and `p`; stripping flags and crate names fixes that without single-letter stop words. AC3 says a routine criterion needs no direct-check clause.

rejected.option: Add `d`, `p` and every crate name to the stop list
rejected.why: Single letters in a stop list let unrelated criteria through.

rejected.option: Skip the whole check when every behavior criterion is routine
rejected.why: AC2 still requires parts (a)-(c) for every code or tests reading with a behavior criterion.

decisions.choice: AC4 on real readings is measured by `loop_replay` (run/mod.rs:2294), which `touches_reading_rules` triggers for a change under crates/, and by the verification replay (`replay_stage`). The producer reads the send-back. If the share is above 35% (30% plus 5 points) it loosens no marker, label or stop list, and writes the measured share and newly refused job ids into its report summary. The fixture replay test `behavior_test_replay_stays_within_the_declared_share` is kept and commented in the code as a mechanics test only: it shows docs, feature and content-only readings are never newly refused, that the declaration parses to 30%, and that the hold rule applies. It is not evidence of the bound.
decisions.reason: The ten fixtures are chosen by the author, so they cannot speak for recent accepted readings. The producer snapshot has no `records/` (system facts), so only `loop_replay` and the verification replay can measure the share. AC4 says markers are not loosened and the share and ids are reported.

rejected.why: `records/` is absent from the producer snapshot.

risks.risk: The real newly refused share may be above 35%. Most past code readings used a one-line survey, so every code or tests reading with a behavior criterion is newly refused.
risks.mitigation: `loop_replay` measures it on real accepted readings during the producer's work. If it is above 35%, no marker, label or stop list is loosened, and the share and the newly refused job ids go into the producer report. The 30% is declared with the reason sentence the replay rules require above 25%. Reusing `Existing code:` for (b) lowers the share a little.

risks.risk: Lexical skip-switch matching misses other names and prose descriptions, refuses some honest phrasings (`no probe runs when skip_probe is set`, `faster than skip_probe`), and can accept a phrase that is only superficially negated by a coordinated list.
risks.mitigation: The closed list, the list-carrying negation rule and the pinned false cases are stated in the doc comment and the CHANGELOG. Corpus cases pin accepted forms (single and coordinated negation, `skip_note`) and refused forms.

risks.risk: The command removal for (d) is lexical: an unbackticked sentence that mixes a command and a function name after the word `cargo` in the same clause loses the function name and is refused.
risks.mitigation: The error names (d) and gives an example clause, and the clause removal ends at `;` or a sentence end, so a function named in a later clause counts. The limit is stated under Limits.

risks.risk: The routine-criterion stop list may miss other wordings of a routine criterion, which would then need a `Direct check:` clause.

risks.risk: Many reading.rs and corpus fixtures use the short survey and would be newly refused. A missed site fails the test suite.

demonstrations.method: Two layers. Layer 1 measures the share on real readings: the producer loop runs `loop_replay` (run/mod.rs:2294) after each parsed report, because the change touches crates/; it replays the newest accepted records with the real `check_reading_text` on both builds and sends the share and the newly refused list back; the verification replay (`replay_stage`, replay.json) reuses it. Fixtures: docs, feature and content-only readings and code readings with a one-line `Code survey:` and a behavior criterion. It asserts the newly refused ids are exactly the code behavior readings, that docs, feature and content-only readings are never newly refused, that the declaration parses to 30, and that the hold rule is true with no declared share and false with 30.
